guarantees.claim: mode is always driven to the value reg2hw_ctrl_i.mode.q cast to aes_mode_e.
key_len is always driven to the value reg2hw_ctrl_i.key_len.q cast to key_len_e.
ctrl_wd.sideload is always equal to reg2hw_ctrl_i.sideload.q.
prng_reseed_rate is always driven to the value reg2hw_ctrl_i.prng_reseed_rate.q cast to prs_rate_e.
phase_o is always the bitwise OR of phase_operation, phase_mode, phase_key_len, phase_key_sideload, phase_prng_reseed_rate, and phase_manual_operation.

assumptions.claim: The input fields reg2hw_ctrl_i.mode.q, reg2hw_ctrl_i.key_len.q, and reg2hw_ctrl_i.prng_reseed_rate.q hold encodings within their respective enumerated types (aes_mode_e, key_len_e, prs_rate_e).
assumptions.cond: always, as the assignments are continuous
assumptions.risk: If any field carries an out-of-range value, the type cast may produce an undefined enum member, causing the downstream AES core to operate in an unknown mode, incorrect key length, or illegal reseed timing, potentially compromising cryptographic operations or exposing secret data.

uncertain_points.claim: The unvalidated type casts expose mode, key_len, and prng_reseed_rate to potentially illegal enum values from the shadow register input. No local hardening guarantees that downstream logic will safely handle out-of-range encodings.
uncertain_points.cond: if reg2hw_ctrl_i fields are corrupted or set to an undefined value
uncertain_points.risk: The AES core could execute with an unanticipated configuration, leading to key leakage, incorrect encryption/decryption, or a deadlock in the reseeding PRNG.

uncertain_points.claim: phase_o is the OR of a specific set of phase signals. If any additional source of phase activity exists outside this list, phase_o would not reflect it, potentially causing the system to misinterpret completion status.
uncertain_points.cond: when the set of phase sources is extended elsewhere without updating this OR
uncertain_points.risk: The top-level controller may prematurely deassert an ongoing condition or miss a busy indicator, causing protocol violations or spurious operations.
